A few months ago, the MacBook Neo took the tech world by storm, becoming the best value laptop of 2026. Even after its recent price increase, it remains most people's top recommendation for an entry-level laptop. Like other great-value Apple products, they’ve added a playful range of colors to this MacBook—think citrus, coral, indigo, and silver—injecting a bit of personality and color into these otherwise standard machines. However, one of my complaints is that most MacBook accessories come in the traditional silver or space gray. Satechi is filling that gap with a new accessory lineup in three colors designed to match the MacBook Neo.

I’ve actually reviewed the “big brother” version of this product before and loved it. This is the most versatile accessory in the new Satechi lineup. It turns one of your USB-C ports into 5 additional ports, and it’s perfectly sized—about the size of a hockey puck—while also featuring MagSafe. So you can use it with your MacBook Neo and your iPhone. This USB-C hub offers the following:

  • HDMI output supporting 4K video at up to 60Hz
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 60W
  • USB-C port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • USB-A port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • Full-size SD card reader
  • Includes a premium braided nylon USB-C cable

Because it has MagSafe, they include a stick-on magnetic ring that you can attach to the lid of your MacBook Neo. And it even comes in a metallic color that matches the Neo! Even when you’re not using the adapter, the magnetic ring doesn’t look out of place. As I mentioned, this is my personal favorite product because it’s incredibly versatile. It’s compact, well-built, includes the essential ports most people need, and is compatible with multiple devices.

The OntheGo Multiport Adapter is available in the same color options as the MacBook Neo and is now on sale at Amazon and Satechi’s website for $44.99.

This one has the more familiar traditional USB-C hub form factor. It snaps directly onto the side of the MacBook Neo (hence the name “Snap Hub”) and adds six new ports—one more than the OntheGo hub mentioned above. You can tell at a glance that it’s designed specifically for the MacBook Neo because it fits so securely. The Snap Hub offers the following:

  • SD and MicroSD card readers
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 45W (more than enough to charge the MacBook Neo, which only supports up to 30W)

The Snap Hub is undoubtedly the most seamlessly integrated of the three accessories in terms of design. It looks and feels like a product Apple themselves would have made. It features a two-tone design: the top perfectly matches the Neo’s material and color, while the rest of the body is cleverly wrapped in a soft-touch rubber material, because they knew this part would be resting against the Neo’s metal chassis—and metal rubbing against metal is generally not ideal. I think this is a brilliant design decision. One thing to note is that this hub will occupy two of the Neo’s USB-C ports, but the hub itself still provides two USB-C ports as well as an additional…

The USB-C Snap Hub is available in the four Neo colors mentioned above and is now on sale. It’s also priced at $44.99, same as the OntheGo multiport adapter, and is available on Amazon and Satechi’s website.

To round out Satechi’s brand-new Neo lineup, they’ve redesigned the Slim EX mouse to match the rest of the collection’s color palette. I’ve used the non-colored version of this mouse before, and it became one of my most recommended products thanks to its incredible value. At $29, you get:

  • Connect up to 3 different devices simultaneously—two via Bluetooth and one via a 2.4GHz receiver (and it’s a USB-C receiver!)
  • Aluminum body
  • USB-C charging
  • User-replaceable battery
  • Up to 3 months of continuous use, with over a year of standby time
  • Includes a USB-C cable for charging and connectivity

The build quality and feel of this mouse absolutely meet the standard you’d expect from a mouse costing twice the price. It features a premium low-profile aluminum body that remains comfortable even during extended use. The ability to quickly switch between multiple devices is incredibly practical for me, as I frequently switch between my MacBook and iPad. Additionally, the 2.4GHz receiver uses USB-C instead of USB-A—an upgrade that is seriously underrated. Even though the Neo’s trackpad is already excellent, I personally still like using both a trackpad and a mouse at the same time. I use the trackpad for gestures and horizontal scrolling, while the mouse is for more precise…

The Slim EX Wireless Mouse is available in the four colors mentioned above, as well as the previously released black version. The mouse is priced at $29.99 and is now available on Amazon and Satechi’s website. If you’re looking to save a bit of money, the black version is actually the same mouse and is currently on sale for just $23.99.

Conclusion

Satechi is the first brand to launch color-matched accessories for the MacBook Neo, and they clearly understand their target audience. They’ve delivered high-quality, practical accessories for the MacBook Neo lineup, compensating for some of the compromises made to keep this $699 laptop affordable. All the accessories are well-crafted, offer plenty of genuinely useful features, and enhance the overall MacBook Neo experience.

If I had to pick one of these products, I’d lean slightly toward the OntheGo Multiport Adapter purely for its versatility and the fact that it works with any device that has a USB-C port and MagSafe. However, the Snap Hub is equally impressive, with a near-perfect physical integration with the Neo, and the Slim EX mouse is a nice bonus. What do you think? Are these accessories worth picking up? Does color-matching matter to you? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments below!
